authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: The complete response contains mar(i) “die” plus the perfective go auxiliary, in that order. CDIAL 9871 supplies the regional mar stem (its deeper Vedic history remains debated); 4008,1 gives gaya/gaa, Hindi gayā, Gujarati gyau/giu and the extended gel forms. Platts explicitly records mar-jānā “die”. The links identify both members of the regional compound, not an inherited Sanskrit compound. Paired elicitation glosses are retained; selected responses contain the affirmative past form, with no unrepresented negative word. Mixed responses and unclear additional material are excluded.

proposals.evidence: This is mār “kill” followed by diyā/diyo “gave” as a perfective auxiliary. CDIAL 10066 supplies the causative kill stem, while specifically 6140,3 *dita supplies Hindi diyā and Kumaoni/Nepali diyo; the contracted dyo retains the same auxiliary. Platts explicitly lists mār-denā as an intensive of mārnā. Both ordered component families are represented; the source paired gloss does not imply that a negative particle occurs in these affirmative responses.

proposals.evidence: The response is khā “eat” plus le/lo or liyo “take” as auxiliary. Platts explicitly records khā-lenā; CDIAL 3865 supplies the bare eating stem, and 10948 gives le with Old Marwari perfect liyo and explains the analogical interaction of take, give and lead. Both ordered components are retained, including the imperative/past inflection of the auxiliary. Mixed slash responses and longer unanalysed auxiliaries are excluded.
